markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

Starting-point insights: (1) Historical scores of 0.5238 for recent-residual/CE and 0.5050 for SASRec motivate replication; they do not isolate component effects. (2) User feedback identifies stale isolated evidence and broad resemblance without a current connection. Recent context targets both, without establishing compatibility or reducing ownership redundancy. (3) Electronics has 20.2% sampled training reversals and a −0.7499 tenth-percentile margin; these justify objective experiments without diagnosing generalization failure.

Related-work insights: (1) SASRec [1] motivates retaining global context; Residual Dominance [5] cautions that additional mixing can reduce accuracy. (2) ScaleRec [2] motivates multiple horizons, but does not establish superiority over five-item pooling. (3) RepeatNet and Repetition and Exploration [6,7] distinguish useful repetition from repetitive bias. (4) NISER [8] motivates examining embedding norms; its session-based findings do not establish the appropriate SASRec normalization. (5) Loss comparisons [3,4,9] require separating negative count from objective choice.

### Framework and candidate ideas

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed test | Unresolved gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Context | SASRec; five-item residual | Fixed versus adaptive 1/5/20-item pools | Context selection versus last-item dominance |
| Discrimination | Single-negative BCE | Matched 64-negative BCE versus CE | Objective versus negative-count effects |
| Specificity | ID associations | From-scratch title fusion | Lexical resemblance versus usefulness |

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty. Each assessment includes a strength and limitation.

| Idea | Assessments: score (+strength; −limitation) |
|---|---|
| **A. Controlled multi-scale residual + CE** [1–9] | O 3 (+diagnosis-guided test; −established components); P 6 (+falsifiable context hypothesis; −incremental); U 7 (+stale and broad-interest failures; −specificity unverified); M 8 (+negative competition; −in-sample rationale); D 5 (+small modules; −controls and sampler coordination) |
| B. Five-item residual + gBCE [1,4] | O 2 (+clear comparator; −standard components); P 6 (+objective evidence; −transfer uncertain); U 6 (+current-context route; −fixed scope); M 8 (+separation test; −calibration unproven); D 4 (+simple loss; −exact weighting essential) |
| C. Gated title/description fusion + recent pooling [1] | O 4 (+permitted content; −known fusion); P 7 (+sparse-item support; −weak supervision); U 7 (+identification and recency; −lexical shortcuts); M 5 (+shared evidence; −indirect mechanism); D 6 (+local training; −tokenization/inference cost) |

### Selected experiment

At 10% progress, retain A as a staged experiment. Add a small scalar-gated projection of causal raw-embedding pools over 1, 5 and 20 items, preserving baseline normalization. This targets stale isolated influence and broad recommendations lacking current support; CE targets measured Electronics separation. These remain hypotheses, and repetition or embedding magnitude could create shortcuts.

Prespecify baseline, CE-only, residual-only and combined comparisons. Prioritize matched-negative BCE/CE and fixed-five controls before attributing gains to adaptive scales; retain baseline eligibility. Additional last-item, fixed-mixture and global-mixture controls require measured remaining budget. Select by pinned macro sampled validation HR@10, record every attempt, and report category results, reversals, gates and branch norms. Adaptive selection requires improvement over fixed controls. Conditional paired-user intervals, when host hits are available, exclude selection bias and training-seed uncertainty [10–12]. No history-sensitivity result or embedding-collapse claim is established.

idea.description: Evaluate a lightweight multi-scale recent-interest residual with uniform multi-negative candidate cross-entropy in per-dataset SASRec through a prespecified, budgeted sequence of comparisons. Retain baseline, objective-only, residual-only and combined configurations, with matched-negative loss and fixed-context controls required for component attribution. Allow baseline or a simpler completed configuration to win.
idea.motivation: The idea explicitly targets two user-facing failures: older isolated interactions outweighing recent repeated activity, and broad associations displacing recommendations with a specific current connection. Causal recent pools supply current-context evidence, while multiple windows test whether a single five-item horizon is unnecessarily restrictive. This is an indirect mechanism for specificity: recent pooling can reinforce broad associations and cannot establish equipment compatibility, complementarity, replacement need, or satisfied demand. Multi-negative competition targets the model-facing Electronics weakness of 20.2% sampled training reversals and a negative lower-tail margin. These in-sample observations do not establish a generalization bottleneck. Historical scores of 0.5238 and 0.5050 motivate replication but do not identify architectural or objective contributions.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve separate models and explicit routing for Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl. Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, unchanged input splits, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and the effective SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Use one GPU and save checkpoints, manifests, diagnostics and predictor artifacts beneath the trial directory. Do not obtain additional datasets or pretrained weights. Only public histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions are permitted; reviews, item categories, ratings, prices, stores and simulator traits remain unavailable despite the generic examples in the input.

Before launching work, obtain the actual remaining shared GPU budget and profile representative training and diagnostic costs. All attempts, failures and diagnostics consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second allocation. Freeze a feasible configuration list, execution order, checkpoint rule, validation-query schedule and stopping rule before new validation exposure. Do not assume that the full initial budget remains. Never select from incomplete four-category configurations. Record failures and partial work rather than reporting missing categories as zero. Preserve the baseline checkpoint rule exactly; if none exists, use the final configured epoch. Fix architecture and optimizer settings from the supplied baseline rather than inventing baseline values. Record their concrete values, software versions, hardware, batch size, sequence length, epoch/step counts, temperature 1, and checkpoint identifiers in the manifest.

Architecture: at each valid position t, compute raw tied item-embedding means over causal windows 1, 5 and 20, excluding padding and dividing by the valid count. Windows count interaction occurrences, so repeated items contribute repeatedly. Short prefixes use their available events. Compute three softmax mixture weights from an affine map of the concatenated unchanged SASRec feature and three pools; initialize all mixture-map parameters to zero, yielding an equal mixture. Apply a bias-free Xavier-initialized projection to that mixture. Add it to the unchanged normalized SASRec feature through a scalar sigmoid gate whose weights start at zero and bias at −2. Add no post-fusion normalization. Explicitly re-zero the padding embedding after generic initialization and keep it fixed. Preserve baseline normalization, optimizer and regularization in primary comparisons. The initial small residual is not an exact identity initialization; retain an explicit no-residual comparator.

Prespecify the primary factorial comparison: unchanged baseline, CE-only, adaptive-residual-only and combined. These estimate the effect of an objective/sampling package, residual addition and their interaction only when all four complete. They cannot isolate loss choice because baseline BCE uses one negative. Prioritize a matched 64-negative balanced-BCE comparator and a fixed-five residual comparator before making loss-specific or adaptive-scale claims. Match their backbone, optimizer, steps, temperature and sampled candidate IDs to the relevant CE or adaptive configuration. A practical fixed order is baseline, CE-only, matched-negative BCE-only, fixed-five-plus-CE, adaptive-plus-CE, and adaptive-residual-only, admitting only the prefix of this list that the measured budget supports. Freeze that feasible prefix before validation. If later controls cannot fit, report only the narrower supported comparisons.

Additional context controls, only if prespecified and affordable, are a last-item residual, an equal fixed mixture of windows 1/5/20, and a global learned softmax mixture whose logits do not depend on the sequence. Use the same projection, residual-gate architecture and initialization wherever applicable. The last-item and five-item controls use their respective pool in place of the mixture. Adaptive scale selection is supported only by favorable comparisons against fixed-five, equal-mixture and global-mixture controls; a combined-versus-baseline gain alone is insufficient. Extra comparisons increase validation-selection exposure and must not trigger an open-ended search.

Sampling and objectives: retain user identity inside the sampler while preserving the required external loader tuple. Uniformly sample without replacement up to 64 unique nonpadding catalog IDs outside each user's complete training history, using only training histories for exclusions. Share this set across that user's sequence positions. For a target not contained in the recorded training history, explicitly remove its ID from that position's candidate set rather than assuming collision freedom. Cap the negative count at the eligible pool size; skip and count users with no eligible negatives. Pad variable-size sets with invalid IDs and mask their CE logits to negative infinity. CE is logsumexp([s_positive, valid_negative_scores]) minus s_positive, averaged across valid positions. It is uncorrected candidate discrimination, not an unbiased full-catalog softmax estimator. Shared negatives preserve each position's marginal draw distribution but induce dependence across positions.

For matched balanced BCE, use softplus(−s_positive) + sum(valid_mask * softplus(s_negative))/K_valid, then average over valid positions. This is distinct from summed-negative BCE and gBCE. Use identical negative IDs for the matched BCE/CE comparison, obtained from a deterministic user/epoch/occurrence-keyed schedule or a recorded sampler stream. A gBCE follow-up must preserve its cited weighting, calibration parameter and definition of sampling probability; do not silently substitute balanced BCE or reuse a catalog-wide probability after history-conditioned exclusions. Do not launch that follow-up until its sampling interpretation is explicitly resolved and its cost fits the remaining budget.

Reproducibility: isolate model/dropout, data-order, negative-sampling, diagnostic and bootstrap random streams. Use explicit DataLoader generators and deterministic worker initialization. Construct baseline backbone parameters before residual parameters so adding the branch does not change initial backbone weights, and verify equality for matched runs. Identical seeds still do not guarantee identical stochastic trajectories across architectures or platforms. Record RNG states and determinism settings; diagnostics must not consume training RNG state. Follow PyTorch reproducibility guidance without changing benchmark seeds.

Confounds and shortcuts: raw repeated occurrences can amplify repetitive bias; tied embedding norms can introduce popularity effects; the one-item pool can dominate without useful contextual mixing. Track training-item popularity, item-embedding norms, branch/base norm ratios, scale weights and gate saturation. For magnitude controls, first measure scales on fixed training-only prefixes. A separately declared norm-matched ablation may rescale each nonzero pool to the same detached baseline-feature norm before mixing, and the projected residual to that norm before gating, with zero-safe handling; retain the raw-pooling primary comparison. A separately budgeted normalized-scoring ablation must change training and inference consistently and specify temperature in advance. Neither control is permission to tune normalization alongside every other component.

Use bounded training-only diagnostic panels to compare unchanged histories with last-item-preserving earlier-context shuffles and earlier duplicate-removal interventions. Keep the last occurrence and final conditioning item when removing duplicates. Report that compaction changes positions and context length; without verified per-layer key/value masks and explicit survivor positions these are not position-controlled causal interventions. Do not alter official splits or infer intent boundaries from perturbation sensitivity. Stratify descriptively by training-history length, repeated-event fraction and target training-popularity bins using prespecified training-derived thresholds, reporting denominators. Validation strata require host-exposed outcomes and authorized metadata; otherwise mark them unavailable.

Select among completed configurations using the host's unchanged pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 with 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. Describe it specifically as sampled HR@10; its ordering need not transfer to full-catalog ranking. Break exact macro ties by the unchanged baseline first, then fewer added components, then predeclared configuration order. Retain all trial results and query counts. If the host exposes per-user hits, run 2,000 paired bootstrap replicates with an isolated seed-42 generator, resampling users within each category and applying identical indices to both models, then averaging category differences equally. Report percentile intervals conditional on fixed models and candidate sets. These exclude training-seed and candidate-sampling uncertainty and do not remove adaptive-selection bias. Do not recreate or modify the evaluator to obtain missing hit vectors. Keep the twenty real training users' full-catalog qualitative assessment separate from benchmark selection; ambiguous items are not demonstrated dislikes.

Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py restores identical windows, projection, mixture and residual gates, scoring normalization if used, model configuration, checkpoint and all four routes. Verify that arbitrary candidate batches and full-catalog chunks produce the same item scores within a prespecified numerical tolerance, using eval mode and fixed histories. Check causal prefix consistency, padding behavior and restoration parity as targeted implementation checks.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Expose the actual trained nn.Module as view.model, its item embeddings as view.item_emb, fused features through log2feats, and consistent predict_score behavior. Preserve user_train, meta_data and review_data compatibility without fabricating unavailable fields. Use an explicit dataset_name or diagnostic_views mapping; local item IDs cannot establish dataset routing. The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B×L tensors. In eval mode without gradients, score each valid target pair from the causal feature at its corresponding position, excluding padding and invalid IDs; restore the prior model training state afterward. Return metrics and metric_definitions, including valid-pair counts, mean scores, mean and nearest-rank tenth-percentile margin, fraction margin<0, fraction margin<0.5, and pairwise accuracy P(margin>0)+0.5P(margin=0). Also report scale-weight distributions, gate saturation using declared thresholds of below 0.05 or above 0.95, and residual/base norm ratios where the base norm is nonzero. Raw-margin comparisons across objectives depend on score scale; sampled training probes do not establish validation performance. The mapped embedding-similarity score measures directional alignment rather than rank collapse or recommendation diversity. Unsupported category metadata, unresolved routing and unmeasured perturbations must remain explicitly unavailable. The interpreter prompt must contain actual measurements, their definitions, data scope, exclusions and limitations.

originality.positive: The diagnosis-guided experiment combines context-scale selection and candidate discrimination with controls that can distinguish several competing explanations.
originality.negative: Multi-scale pooling, gates, residual branches and sampled CE are established; better controls strengthen evidence rather than architectural novelty.

future_potential.positive: Evidence beyond fixed-five, equal-mixture and global-mixture controls could motivate more principled context selection and recurring-interest modeling.
future_potential.negative: Benefits remain unmeasured, and adaptive weights cannot establish intent boundaries, compatibility or functional usefulness. The extension is incremental.

code_difficulty.positive: The neural branch is small and uses ordinary PyTorch pooling, affine maps and existing item scoring.
code_difficulty.negative: Matched sampling, reproducible initialization, variable-count masking, budgeted controls, predictor parity and architecture-aware diagnostics add substantial coordination beyond the branch itself.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal attention-based sequential recommendation baseline and item-scoring mechanism.
Supports retaining contextual history rather than assuming a last-item-only representation suffices.
limitations: Does not establish equipment compatibility, complementarity or satisfaction of an already owned function.
Its contextual-attention evidence does not establish adaptive pooling gains on the matched benchmark.

related_work.title: ScaleRec
contributions: The supplied search summary describes multi-granularity history patches, local and inter-patch attention, and adaptive signal filtering.
limitations: Does not establish learned intent boundaries or gains for the proposed lightweight pooling adaptation.
Does not demonstrate superiority over a five-item residual in this task.

related_work.title: Comparison of Recommendation Loss Functions
contributions: Analyzes BCE, categorical cross-entropy and BPR, distinguishing full-catalog and sampled objectives.
limitations: Does not establish a universally superior sampled loss or validate the proposed combination.
Full-catalog ranking bounds cannot be transferred directly to uncorrected sampled-candidate CE.

related_work.title: gSASRec: Generalised Binary Cross-Entropy for Sequential Recommendations
contributions: Provides a calibrated multi-negative BCE alternative.
Motivates examining the effects of negative sampling and positive/negative loss weighting.
limitations: Reported evidence does not cover these four matched Amazon categories.
Exact weighting and sampling assumptions must be preserved; balanced multi-negative BCE is a different objective.

related_work.title: Residual Dominance
contributions: The supplied search summary reports substantially weaker effects from earlier-item shuffling when the last item is preserved.
Shows that recovering some context-dependent misses can accompany lower overall accuracy.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed residual improves contextual reasoning.
Additional contextual mixing cannot be assumed to improve aggregate ranking.

related_work.title: RepeatNet: A Repeat Aware Neural Recommendation Machine for Session-based Recommendation
contributions: Separates repeat and exploration behavior.
Motivates reporting repeated-target and non-repeat behavior separately where authorized outcomes permit.
limitations: Session-based repeat-consumption gains need not transfer to unseen-item recommendation.
Repeated history evidence does not establish a need to purchase another functionally similar item.

related_work.title: Repetition and Exploration in Sequential Recommendation
contributions: The supplied search summary identifies repetitive bias and sensitivity to shared input/output embeddings.
limitations: Does not determine whether retaining or downweighting repeated events is best for these datasets.
Supports diagnostic controls rather than a guaranteed correction.

related_work.title: NISER: Normalized Item and Session Representations to Handle Popularity Bias
contributions: Links embedding magnitudes with popularity bias in session-based recommendation.
Motivates norm measurements and explicitly controlled normalization ablations.
limitations: Does not establish the appropriate normalization for SASRec residual pooling.
Changing scoring normalization also changes optimization and must be treated as a separate intervention.

related_work.title: Controlled SASRec implementation accompanying Revisiting Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides precedent for multiple unseen negatives per user shared across sequence positions.
Supports an efficient implementation of candidate cross-entropy.
limitations: Shared negatives correlate position-level samples.
The implementation precedent does not make uncorrected candidate CE equivalent to full-catalog CE or prove superiority on this task.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can yield different model orderings from full-catalog metrics.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned benchmark.
Its warning limits the interpretation of sampled HR@10 rather than invalidating the required selection protocol.

related_work.title: Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
contributions: Provides a paired bootstrap resampling precedent adaptable to paired user outcomes within categories.
limitations: The proposed category-stratified recommendation bootstrap is an adaptation.
Conditional bootstrap intervals do not account for training randomness, candidate sampling or validation selection.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit validation criteria.
Motivates prespecified comparisons, complete trial accounting and restricted validation exposure.
limitations: Does not provide a correction that makes adaptively selected validation gains unbiased.
A single fixed training seed remains insufficient to establish robustness.

related_work.title: PyTorch Reproducibility Notes
contributions: Documents random-stream control, DataLoader worker seeding and deterministic execution considerations.
Clarifies reproducibility limits across releases and platforms.
limitations: Identical seeds do not ensure identical stochastic trajectories across different architectures.
Deterministic settings can affect runtime and must be included in budget estimates.
